name: EUV lithography machines
what_it_is: The only machines in the world that print the finest circuit patterns on chips, made solely by ASML.
used_for: Making the most advanced AI chips (below roughly 5nm) at scale.
status_detail: No EUV machine has been shipped to China; Dutch and US controls bar it. Press coverage describes China as roughly a decade or more away from its own EUV tool.
evidence: ASML is the world's only EUV maker; UBS analysts put China's gap at at least a decade (as reported by Asiae/Bloomberg-derived coverage).

sources.title: Zeiss/ASML EUV coverage (Asiae, Zeiss semiconductor CEO)
ASML caught between US and China over MATCH Act (IO+)

name: ASML DUV immersion lithography and servicing
what_it_is: Older-generation chip printing machines that, used repeatedly, can still make fairly advanced chips.
used_for: Making 7nm-class chips for Huawei AI processors and most mature-node chips in China.
status_detail: The most advanced DUV immersion tools need Dutch licenses; older DUV tools still sell. The pending US MATCH Act (introduced April 2026, not passed as of Oct 2026) would extend controls to DUV and possibly servicing; the Dutch government opposes it.
evidence: China was 36% of ASML sales in 2024 and 33% in 2025 (its largest market); ASML guides to about 20% in 2026.
contested_note: ASML and the Dutch government argue broader curbs speed Chinese self-reliance and hurt allied firms; US hawks say they are needed to stop 7nm/5nm expansion.

name: Zeiss lithography optics
what_it_is: Ultra-precise mirrors and lenses that focus light inside chip-printing machines.
used_for: Building EUV and DUV lithography machines; China has no equivalent supplier.
status_detail: Zeiss supplies ASML, not China directly; its EUV optics are exclusive to ASML and fall under the EUV ban. Destination shown is the Chinese lithography maker that lacks such optics; this is a leverage illustration, not a direct shipment line. Zeiss opposes broader curbs.
evidence: Coverage of ASML's 2025 annual report calls Zeiss the exclusive EUV optics supplier; Zeiss SMT executives call a 15-year Chinese timeline reasonable.

name: Etch, deposition and coating tools
what_it_is: Machines that carve and coat silicon wafers; Tokyo Electron is a world leader.
used_for: Fabricating logic and memory chips, including chips for AI hardware.
status_detail: Japan has controlled 23 categories of advanced chipmaking equipment since July 2023, with more items added in 2025. Most tool sales to non-listed Chinese customers still flow legally. The US MATCH Act proposal would pressure Japan to go further and may cover servicing.
evidence: China was 34.1% of Tokyo Electron revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026, falling to 26.8% in the final quarter.
contested_note: Japanese firms say further curbs cost them sales without stopping Chinese progress.

name: Photoresist and high-purity chemicals
what_it_is: Light-sensitive coatings and ultra-pure chemicals used to print patterns on wafers; Japanese firms dominate.
used_for: Every step of chip lithography, including advanced nodes.
status_detail: No formal Japanese ban confirmed. In Nov 2025 social media rumors said Japan had halted photoresist shipments to China amid the Takaichi dispute; no government or company confirmed it. Current 2026 status unverified.
evidence: Four Japanese firms held 72.5% of global photoresist in 2021; Chinese domestic substitution estimated below 5% (TrendForce). Shin-Etsu halted deliveries to China briefly in 2021.
contested_note: China says it can find domestic and foreign alternatives; Japanese firms deny a halt.

name: TSMC leading-edge chip manufacturing
what_it_is: The world's best contract chip factory; Chinese AI chip designers cannot match its quality.
status_detail: US foundry due-diligence rule (Jan 2025) requires fabs to vet customers for 16/14nm and below; TSMC stopped shipping 7nm-and-below AI chips to many Chinese designers. Taiwan also put Huawei and SMIC on its export blacklist. Current enforcement status not re-verified for late 2026.
evidence: TSMC made about $500 million of wafers for Sophgo that ended up in Huawei's Ascend 910B; a $1B+ US fine was reportedly considered.

name: TSMC chips diverted via Sophgo
what_it_is: Advanced TSMC chip dies bought by a front customer and passed on to Huawei for its AI processors.
status_detail: Discovered in 2024; TSMC cut off Sophgo and the US tightened foundry rules in Jan 2025. A Commerce fine over $1B was reported under consideration; outcome not verified.
evidence: TechInsights identified TSMC N7HPC dies in the Ascend 910B; about $500M of wafers were made for Sophgo.

name: High-bandwidth memory (HBM)
what_it_is: Stacked memory chips placed next to an AI processor to feed it data fast; only SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron make it at scale.
used_for: Training and running frontier AI models.
status_detail: US rules from 2 Dec 2024 restrict HBM sales to China. Chinese firms stockpiled Samsung HBM2E before the rule. China's CXMT is reported to be working toward its own HBM3 (2026-27). Current license practice not fully verified.
evidence: China was about 30% of Samsung HBM revenue in the first half of 2024, before the curbs (Reuters, as relayed).

name: Korean memory fabs inside China (VEU ended)
what_it_is: Samsung and SK Hynix run big memory factories in China (Xi'an, Wuxi, Dalian) that depend on imported US-origin tools.
used_for: A large share of world DRAM and NAND memory; China-based output is a source of Chinese supply.
status_detail: US revoked the validated end-user waivers for these fabs (announced Aug 29, 2025; effective end of 2025). In late Dec 2025 the US reportedly granted annual licenses for 2026 covering Xi'an, Wuxi and Dalian, limited to keeping existing operations running, no expansion or upgrades. 2027 license outcome not confirmed.
evidence: BIS estimated the change would generate over 1,000 additional license applications per year.
contested_note: Korean industry warns it forfeits market space to Chinese rivals; US officials want to freeze Chinese-site capability.

name: SK Hynix Wuxi DRAM fab
what_it_is: SK Hynix's main Chinese DRAM plant, supplied with tools and know-how from Korea and abroad.
used_for: Roughly a large share of SK Hynix's DRAM output, supplying PCs, phones and servers.
status_detail: Same VEU revocation and annual 2026 license as other Korean China fabs: operations may continue but upgrades are not approved. Details of any 2027 renewal not confirmed.
evidence: Annual 2026 license covers Wuxi DRAM and Dalian NAND, per Reuters as relayed.

name: TSMC advanced packaging (CoWoS)
what_it_is: A way of stacking processor and memory chips together on one base; TSMC's version is the industry standard for AI chips.
status_detail: No CoWoS-specific rule confirmed; access is blocked in practice via the foundry rule and TSMC stopping advanced-node work for Chinese designers. Huawei reportedly uses a Chinese copy of CoWoS-S. Not verified for 2026.
evidence: Analysts found Huawei's Ascend 910B packaging strongly based on TSMC's CoWoS-S.
